answer.text:
With ${\rm M}_{1}$ in the ${\rm C.G.}$ and
${\rm M}_{2}$ in the ${\rm C.S.}$ the circuit is the
shunt-shunt, $V-I$, prototype

$${\rm sample}\;V_{o}\;\;{\rm mix}\;I_{i}\qquad 
\beta =I_{f}/V_{o}$$

with the ${\rm PMOS}$ as the ${\rm VCCS}$ feedback
element.  Put $V_{b}=0$ for $ac$, $V_{DD}=0$ for $ac$,
$r_{o1}=1/g_{ds1}$, $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}$, $r_{oI}=1/g_{oI}$,
$r_{oB}=1/g_{oB}$ for the two $dc$ current sources.
Neglect $C_{gs},C_{gd}$ for the low frequency
analysis.  Body effect is $g_{m}\rightarrow g_{m}+g_{mb}$.

$$\eqalign{
V_{GS1}&=V_{b}-V_{x}\cr
V_{SG2}&=V_{DD}-V_{o}\cr
V_{DS1}&=V_{o}-V_{x}\cr
V_{SD2}&=V_{DD}-V_{x}}$$

$$I_{D1}=I_{1}\tag{1}$$
$$I_{D2}+I_{in}=I_{D1}+I_{B}\tag{2}$$

so that in $dc$

$$V_{x}=V_{b}-V_{GS1}(I_{1})\qquad 
V_{o}=V_{DD}-V_{SG2}(I_{1}+I_{B}-I_{in})$$

and for $ac$ with the usual $g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$
model, Fig.1,

* ${\rm M}_{1}$ : $g_{m1}v_{gs1}$ $D\rightarrow S$,
$v_{gs1}=-v_{x}$, $r_{o1}$ $D-S$
* ${\rm M}_{2}$ : $g_{m2}v_{sg2}$ $S\rightarrow D$,
$v_{sg2}=-v_{o}$, $r_{o2}$ $S-D$

$$\eqalign{
{\rm KCL}_{x}:&-(I_{in})+{{v_{x}-v_{o}}\over {r_{o1}}}
+{{v_{x}}\over {r_{o2}}}+{{v_{x}}\over {r_{oB}}}
-g_{m1}v_{gs1}-g_{m2}v_{sg2}=0\cr
{\rm KCL}_{o}:&{{v_{o}-v_{x}}\over {r_{o1}}}+{{v_{o}}\over {r_{oI}}}
+g_{m1}v_{gs1}=0\tag{3}}$$

i. e.

$$\eqalign{
I_{in}&=v_{x}\left({1\over {r_{o1}}}+{1\over {r_{o2}}}
+{1\over {r_{oB}}}+g_{m1}\right)
+v_{o}\left(g_{m2}-{1\over {r_{o1}}}\right) \tag{4a}\cr
0&=-v_{x}\left({1\over {r_{o1}}}+g_{m1}\right)
+v_{o}\left({1\over {r_{o1}}}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}\right) \tag{4b}}$$

Put

$$G_{1}={1\over {r_{o1}}}+g_{m1}\qquad 
G_{2}={1\over {r_{o1}}}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}\qquad 
A=G_{1}+{1\over {r_{o2}}}+{1\over {r_{oB}}}$$

From (4b)

$$v_{o}=v_{x}{{G_{1}}\over {G_{2}}}\tag{5}$$

the familiar ${\rm C.G.}$ gain

$$A_{v0}={{v_{o}}\over {v_{x}}}\Bigl|_{g_{m2}=0}
={{G_{1}}\over {G_{2}}}={{1+g_{m1}r_{o1}}\over {1+r_{o1}/r_{oI}}}
\approx 1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\;\;r_{oI}\gg r_{o1}$$

on the $r_{oI}\parallel r_{o1}$ load.  With (5) in (4a)

$$I_{in}=v_{o}\left[ G_{2}{{A}\over {G_{1}}}+g_{m2}
-{1\over {r_{o1}}}\right]
=v_{o}\left[ g_{m2}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{{G_{2}}\over {G_{1}}}
\left({1\over {r_{o2}}}+{1\over {r_{oB}}}\right)\right] \tag{6}$$

Hence for $r_{oB}\rightarrow \infty $

$${{V_{o}}\over {I_{in}}}=R_{M}=
{1\over {\,g_{m2}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{{G_{2}}\over {G_{1}r_{o2}}}\,}}
\tag{7}$$

and with the normal $r_{oI},r_{o2}\gg r_{o1}$,

$$R_{M}\approx {1\over {g_{m2}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{1\over
{r_{o2}(1+g_{m1}r_{o1})}}}}\tag{7a}$$

In the ideal $r_{o}\rightarrow \infty $ limit

$$R_{M0}={1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\over {g_{m2}(1+g_{m1}r_{o1})+1/r_{o2}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m2}}}\tag{8}$$

The sign is non inverting for the reference direction in
Fig.24, $R_{M}=-1/\beta $ with $\beta =-g_{m2}$ for the
usual $I_{f}=-g_{m2}V_{o}$ convention.  The ${\rm PMOS}$
is a feedback resistor $R_{F}=1/g_{m2}$.  Replacing
${\rm M}_{2}$ by $R_{F}$ gives the classic resistive
shunt-shunt ${\rm TIA}$ $R_{M}=-R_{F}$.

The forward transimpedance with the feedback $g_{m2}$
killed but with its loading $r_{o2}$ retained is from
(6) with $g_{m2}=0$,

$$R_{M}^{o}={1\over {{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{{G_{2}}\over {G_{1}r_{o2}}}}}
\approx r_{oI}\parallel r_{o1}\tag{9}$$

the ${\rm C.G.}$ $I\rightarrow V$ gain.  The feedback
factor is

$$\beta ={{I_{f}}\over {V_{o}}}=-g_{m2}\tag{10}$$

so that the return ratio, loop gain, is

$$T=-\beta R_{M}^{o}=g_{m2}R_{M}^{o}
={{g_{m2}}\over {{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{{G_{2}}\over {G_{1}r_{o2}}}}}
\approx g_{m2}r_{oI}\;\;r_{o2}\gg r_{o1}\tag{11}$$

More exactly breaking the loop at the high impedance
gate of ${\rm M}_{2}$, $v_{t}$ on the gate, $v_{r}$ at
$V_{o}$,

$${{v_{r}}\over {v_{t}}}}=-{{g_{m2}}\over 
{{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{{G_{2}}\over {G_{1}r_{o2}}}}}\tag{12}$$

so that $T=-v_{r}/v_{t}$ is (11), $T\approx
g_{m2}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{oI})\approx 20-50\,{\rm dB}$.
Then

$$R_{M}={{R_{M}^{o}}\over {1+T}}\approx -{1\over \beta }
={1\over {g_{m2}}}\tag{13}$$

as in (8).  The feedback is negative: $\uparrow I_{in}
\rightarrow \uparrow v_{x}\rightarrow \downarrow v_{gs1}
\rightarrow \downarrow i_{d1}\rightarrow \uparrow v_{o}
\rightarrow \downarrow v_{sg2}\rightarrow \downarrow i_{d2}
\rightarrow \downarrow v_{x}$.

Input impedance, $Z_{in}=v_{x}/I_{in}$,

$$Z_{in}={{G_{2}}\over {G_{1}}}R_{M}
={1\over {{G_{1}}\over {G_{2}}}\left(g_{m2}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}\right)
+{1\over {r_{o2}}}+{1\over {r_{oB}}}}\tag{14}$$

$$\approx {1\over {{1\over {r_{o2}}}+{{G_{1}}\over {G_{2}}}
\left(g_{m2}+{1\over {r_{oI}}}\right)}}\tag{14a}$$

For $r_{oI},r_{oB}\rightarrow \infty $

$$Z_{in}\approx {1\over {g_{m2}(1+g_{m1}r_{o1})+1/r_{o2}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o1}}}\tag{15}$$

i. e. the ${\rm C.G.}$ input resistance
$1/G_{1}\approx 1/g_{m1}$ divided by $1+T$,

$$Z_{in}={{Z_{in}^{o}}\over {1+T}},\qquad 
Z_{in}^{o}\approx {1\over {G_{1}}}\parallel r_{o2}\tag{16}$$

a virtual ground, $10-10^{2}\,\Omega $ typical, ideal
$0$ for $T\rightarrow \infty $.

Output impedance, $I_{in}=0$, $v_{test}=v_{o}$,
$i_{test}$ into $V_{o}$,

$$i_{test}={{v_{o}-v_{x}}\over {r_{o1}}}+{{v_{o}}\over {r_{oI}}}
+g_{m1}v_{gs1}\tag{17}$$

with $v_{x}=-v_{o}(g_{m2}-1/r_{o1})/A$ from (4a) with
$I_{in}=0$,

$$Z_{out}={{v_{o}}\over {i_{test}}}
={1\over {{1\over {r_{oI}}}+{{g_{m2}G_{1}+1/r_{o1}r_{o2}}\over {A}}}}
\tag{18}$$

$$\approx {1\over {{1\over {r_{oI}}}+g_{m2}{{G_{1}}\over {A}}}}
\approx {1\over {g_{m2}+1/r_{oI}}}\approx {1\over {g_{m2}}}
\;\;r_{o2}\gg r_{o1}\tag{18a}$$

i. e.

$$Z_{out}={{Z_{out}^{o}}\over {1+T}},\qquad 
Z_{out}^{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{oI}\tag{19}$$

also lowered by $1+T$ from the high ${\rm C.G.}$ output
resistance to $\sim 1/g_{m2}$, $0.5-2\,{\rm k\Omega }$
typical.  With $g_{mb}$,

$$g_{m1}\rightarrow g_{m1}+g_{mb1},\qquad 
g_{m2}\rightarrow g_{m2}+g_{mb2}\;{\rm if\;body\;not\;to\;source}.$$

Frequency behaviour: dominant pole at the high impedance
output node

$$\omega _{p o}\approx {1\over {Z_{out}^{o}C_{o}}}
\approx {1\over {(r_{o1}\parallel r_{oI})C_{o}}}$$

closed loop $\omega _{p o,cl}\approx (1+T)\omega _{p o}
\approx g_{m2}/C_{o}$, non dominant pole at the low
impedance input node

$$\omega _{p i}\approx {1\over {Z_{in}C_{i}}}
\approx {{g_{m1}g_{m2}r_{o1}}\over {C_{i}}}\gg \omega _{p o}$$

so the loop is normally well compensated with
$>60^{\circ}$ phase margin.  $C_{o}$ is the total
capacitance at $V_{o}$, $C_{i}$ at $V_{x}$.  Peaking
occurs if $C_{o}$ is made small so that
$\omega _{p o,cl}\approx \omega _{p i}$.

In short the circuit is a low $Z_{in}$, low $Z_{out}$
transimpedance amplifier, the active feedback version of
the $R_{F}$ shunt-shunt ${\rm TIA}$, often called the
flipped voltage follower / super ${\rm C.G.}$ / regulated
cascode ${\rm TIA}$, with ideal

$$R_{M}\approx 1/g_{m2},\qquad Z_{in}\approx 0,\qquad 
Z_{out}\approx 1/g_{m2},\qquad T\approx g_{m2}r_{oI}\gg 1$$

and more exactly (7), (14), (18).  It provides a
virtual ground for current input, e. g. photodiode or
current DAC, and a voltage output capable of driving a
moderate load, with bandwidth $\approx g_{m2}/C_{o}$.

With ${\rm M}_{1}$ put ${\rm G}$ to ${\rm ac}$
ground and ${\rm M}_{2}$ put ${\rm S}$ to ${\rm ac}$ ground

$${\rm M}_{1}:{\rm CG}\qquad {\rm M}_{2}:{\rm CS}\qquad 
V_{G1}=V_{b}={\rm ac}\;0\;\;V_{S2}=V_{DD}={\rm ac}\;0$$

$$I_{D1}=I_{1}\tag{1}$$
$$I_{D2}+I_{in}=I_{D1}+I_{B}\tag{2}$$

at the ${\rm O/P}$ node and at the ${\rm I/P}$ node.
For the signal $I_{in}=i_{in}$ put $I_{B}=g_{B}V_{x}$,
$I_{1}=g_{I}V_{out}$,

$$g_{B}=1/R_{B}\;\;g_{I}=1/R_{I}\;\;g_{ds1}=1/r_{o1}\;\;
g_{ds2}=1/r_{o2}$$

$$g_{m1}^{\prime}=g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\tag{3}$$

for the ${\rm NMOS}$ if the bulk is to ground.
For the ${\rm PMOS}$ $g_{mb2}=0$ if $n$ well to $V_{DD}$.

Small signal Fig.1.  $v_{gs1}=-v_{x}$,
$v_{sg2}=-v_{out}$,

$${\rm M}_{1}:I_{M1}=g_{m1}^{\prime}v_{gs1}+g_{ds1}(v_{out}-v_{x})
      =-g_{m1}^{\prime}v_{x}+g_{ds1}(v_{out}-v_{x})\tag{4}$$
directed ${\rm D}\to {\rm S}$, i. e. $v_{out}\to v_{x}$.

$${\rm M}_{2}:I_{M2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}(0-v_{x})
      =-g_{m2}v_{out}-g_{ds2}v_{x}\tag{5}$$
directed ${\rm S}\to {\rm D}$, i. e. $V_{DD}\to v_{x}$.

KCL $v_{x}$ , currents leaving $v_{x}$,

$$\eqalign{
-I_{M1}-I_{M2}+g_{B}v_{x}-i_{in}=0\cr
\left[g_{m1}^{\prime}v_{x}+g_{ds1}(v_{x}-v_{out})\right]
      +\left[g_{m2}v_{out}+g_{ds2}v_{x}\right]+g_{B}v_{x}-i_{in}=0\cr
v_{x}\left(g_{m1}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{B}\right)
      +v_{out}\left(g_{m2}-g_{ds1}\right)=i_{in}\tag{6}}$$

KCL $v_{out}$,

$$I_{M1}+g_{I}v_{out}=0\tag{7}$$
$$-g_{m1}^{\prime}v_{x}+g_{ds1}(v_{out}-v_{x})+g_{I}v_{out}=0$$
$$v_{x}\left(g_{m1}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}\right)-v_{out}\left(g_{ds1}+g_{I}\right)=0\tag{8}$$

$$v_{out}=v_{x}{\displaystyle{g_{m1}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}\over g_{ds1}+g_{I}}}\tag{9}$$

non inverting ${\rm CG}$ gain.  Put (9) in (6)

$$v_{x}=i_{in}{\displaystyle{g_{ds1}+g_{I}\over 
\left(g_{m1}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{B}\right)\left(g_{ds1}+g_{I}\right)
+\left(g_{m2}-g_{ds1}\right)\left(g_{m1}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}\right)}}\tag{10}$$

$${\cal R}_{m}\equiv {v_{out}\over i_{in}}
      ={g_{m1}^{\prime}+g_{ds1}\over

This circuit is a **PMOS common-source amplifier with current-input feedback**, often used as a **transimpedance amplifier (TIA)** or a **current-to-voltage converter**.

Let's break down the circuit and analyze its operation:

---

### **Circuit Components**

- **M₁**: PMOS transistor, acting as the **input device**. Its gate is biased at a fixed voltage `V_b`, and its source is connected to the input current node.
- **M₂**: PMOS transistor, acting as the **amplifying device**. Its gate is connected to the source of M₁ (which is also the input node for `I_in`), and its source is connected to `V_DD`.
- **I₁**: A **current source** (or current sink) connected to the drain of M₂, providing a constant bias current.
- **I_in**: The **input current** to be amplified/converted. It is injected into the common source node of M₁ and M₂.
- **V_out**: The output voltage, taken from the drain of M₂ (and also the drain of M₁, since they are connected).
- **V_DD**: Supply voltage.
- **V_b**: Bias voltage for the gate of M₁.

---

### **Operation Principle**

This is a **feedback amplifier** where the input is a **current** (`I_in`), and the output is a **voltage** (`V_out`). The feedback is implemented through the **source degeneration** of M₂ by M₁.

#### **1. DC Biasing**

- M₁ is biased in saturation by `V_b`. Its drain current `I_D1` is approximately constant (if `V_b` is fixed and M₁ is in saturation).
- M₂ is also biased in saturation. Its gate voltage is set by the source voltage of M₁, which is determined by the input current `I_in` and the characteristics of M₁.

#### **2. Small-Signal Analysis**

Let’s consider small-signal behavior. We assume both transistors are in saturation.

- The input current `I_in` flows into the source of M₂ and the drain of M₁.
- Since M₁ is biased with a fixed `V_b`, its gate-source voltage is fixed, so its drain current `I_D1` is approximately constant (in small-signal, we can consider it as a current source).
- Therefore, any change in `I_in` must be absorbed by M₂’s drain current `I_D2`.

The key insight is that **M₁ provides negative feedback** to M₂:

- If `I_in` increases, the source voltage of M₂ (which is also the drain voltage of M₁) must increase to allow M₂ to sink more current.
- But an increase in the source voltage of M₂ (which is its gate voltage, since M₂’s gate is connected to M₁’s source) will **decrease** the gate-source voltage of M₂ (`V_GS2 = V_G2 - V_S2 = V_S1 - V_S2`), which tends to **reduce** `I_D2`.
- This is **negative feedback**: the circuit opposes the change in `I_in` by adjusting `V_out` to maintain equilibrium.

#### **3. Transimpedance Gain**

The output voltage `V_out` is related to the input current `I_in` by the **transimpedance gain** `Z_T = V_out / I_in`.

In the small-signal model:

- The output resistance at `V_out` is approximately the parallel combination of the output resistances of M₁ and M₂ (`r_o1 || r_o2`), since both transistors are connected in parallel at the output node.
- The transconductance of M₂ is `g_m2`.

> The circuit acts like a **current mirror with feedback**, where the input current `I_in` is mirrored and converted to a voltage by the output resistance.

But more accurately, since M₁ is providing feedback, the transimpedance gain is approximately:

\[
Z_T \approx \frac{1}{g_{m2}} \cdot \left(1 + g_{m2} \cdot r_{o2} \right) \cdot \text{(feedback factor)}
\]

Actually, a more straightforward analysis:

- The input current `I_in` flows through the source of M₂.
- The gate of M₂ is connected to the source of M₁, which is a high-impedance node.
- The output voltage `V_out` is developed across the output resistance of M₂ (and M₁).

In many practical designs, if M₁ and M₂ are matched and biased similarly, the transimpedance gain is approximately:

\[
Z_T \approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}} \quad \text{(if M₁ is acting as a degeneration resistor)}
\]

But this is not entirely accurate.

---

### **Correct Small-Signal Model**

Let’s derive the transimpedance gain properly.

Define:

- `v_in` = small-signal voltage at the source of M₂ (which is also the drain of M₁).
- `i_in` = small-signal input current.
- `v_out` = small-signal output voltage.

The small-signal current through M₁ is:

\[

\]

The small-signal current through M₂ is:

\[

\]

At the output node (drain of M₁ and M₂), KCL gives:

\[
i_{in} = i_{d1} + i_{d2}
\]

Substitute:

\[
i_{in} = \left[ -g_{m1} v_{in} + \frac{v_{out} - v_{in}}{r_{o1}} \right] + \left[ g_{m2} (v_{in} - v_{out}) + \frac{v_{out}}{r_{o2}} \right]

Group terms:

\[

The feedback is **current-series feedback** (or **series-shunt** if you consider the output as voltage).

\[

\[

But `V_{GS2} = V_{G2} - V_{S2} = V_{S1} - V_{out}`

Then:

\[

So:

\[
V_{out} \approx V_{S1} - \frac{I_{in}}{g_{m2}}

Thus, the transimpedance gain is:

\[
\frac{V_{out}}{I_{in}} \approx -\frac{1}{g_{m2}}
\]

This is a key result.

---

### **Conclusion**

- The circuit is a **PMOS transimpedance amplifier**.
- The input current `I_in` is converted to an output voltage `V_out`.
- The transimpedance gain is approximately **-1/g_m2**, where `g_m2` is the transconductance of M₂.
- The negative sign indicates that an increase in `I_in` (sinking current) causes a decrease in `V_out`.
- M₁ provides **negative feedback** by stabilizing the gate voltage of M₂.
- The circuit has **low input impedance** (good for current input) and **high output impedance** (good for driving capacitive loads).

This topology is commonly used in **optical receivers** and **sensor interfaces** where a small current needs to be converted to a voltage with high gain and bandwidth.

---

### **Final Answer**

The circuit is a **PMOS transimpedance amplifier** with current-input feedback. The input current `I_in` is converted to an output voltage `V_out` with a transimpedance gain of approximately **-1/g_m2**, where `g_m2` is the transconductance of transistor M₂. The input is a **current** ($I_{in}$) and the output is a **voltage** ($V_{out}$) → the amplifier is a **transresistance (transimpedance) amplifier**.

Hence the topology is **shunt–shunt (voltage‑shunt) feedback**, which is the correct topology for a current‑in / voltage‑out converter and gives negative feedback (verified below).

* **Forward path:** M1 is a **common‑gate** stage (gate = AC ground, input at source $X$, output at drain $V_{out}$).
* **Feedback path:** M2 is a **common‑source** transconductance element (source = AC ground, gate = $V_{out}$, drain = $X$) that converts $V_{out}$ into a current injected at $X$.

$$-g_{m1}v_x+\frac{v_{out}-v_x}{r_{o1}}=0 \;\Rightarrow\; v_{out}=v_x\,(1+g_{m1}r_{o1}) \tag{1}$$

For $T\gg 1$ (and in the limit $r_o\to\infty$ exactly):

---
## Step 1: Component & Connection Identification
The circuit uses 2 MOSFETs (M1: PMOS, M2: NMOS), 3 current sources, and a bias voltage $V_b$:
1.  **$V_{DD}$**: Top supply rail, connected *only* to the **drain of M2 (NMOS)**.
2.  **M2 (NMOS)**:
    - Source (arrow points *out* of the device, NMOS convention) connected to the $V_{out}$ node.
    - Gate connected to the input node $V_X$.
    - Acts as an active *current source*: it sources fixed current $I_1$ from $V_{DD}$ to $V_{out}$ (drain-to-source current $I_{D2}$).
3.  **$I_1$**: Current sink between $V_{out}$ and ground, sinking current $I_1$ from $V_{out}$ to ground (arrow points down, in the direction of current flow).
4.  **M1 (PMOS)**:
    - Source connected to bias voltage $V_b$.
    - Drain connected to input node $V_X$.
    - Gate connected to $V_{out}$: this is the **negative feedback path** from output to M1's gate.
    - Acts as a current source from $V_b$ to $V_X$, with current $I_{S1D1}$ (source-to-drain, flowing into $V_X$).
5.  **Input Node $V_X$**:
    - Connected to M1's drain, M2's gate, input current source $I_{in}$, and a bias current sink $I_{bias}$.
    - $I_{in}$: Input current source, arrow points up, so current flows *into* $V_X$ from ground.
    - $I_{bias}$: Fixed bias current sink, arrow points down, sinking current from $V_X$ to ground.
---
## Step 2: DC Operating Point Analysis
We assume both transistors operate in the **saturation (active) region** (standard for analog circuits, for high gain/resistance), and ignore channel length modulation (CLM, $\lambda=0$) for hand analysis.
### KCL at $V_{out}$ Node:
Current entering $V_{out}$ from M2 equals current leaving through $I_1$:
$$I_{D2} = I_1 \tag{1}$$
For M2 (NMOS, saturation):
$$I_{D2} = \frac{1}{2} k_{n2} \left(V_{GS2} - V_{th2}\right)^2$$
Where:
- $V_{GS2} = V_X - V_{out}$ (gate voltage minus source voltage, $V_{S2}=V_{out}$),
- $k_{n2} = \mu_n C_{ox} \frac{W}{L}$ for M2, $V_{th2}>0$ is M2's threshold voltage.
Substitute into (1) and solve for $V_X - V_{out}$:
$$V_X - V_{out} = V_{th2} + \sqrt{\frac{2I_1}{k_{n2}}} \tag{2}$$
This is a **fixed DC offset** between $V_X$ and $V_{out}$, set by $I_1$ and M2's parameters, independent of the input current $I_{in}$.
---
### KCL at Input Node $V_X$:
Currents entering $V_X$: $I_{in}$ and M1's source-to-drain current $I_{S1D1}$. Current leaving: $I_{bias}$:
$$I_{in} + I_{S1D1} = I_{bias} \implies I_{S1D1} = I_{bias} - I_{in} \tag{3}$$
For M1 (PMOS, saturation):
$$I_{S1D1} = \frac{1}{2} k_{p1} \left(V_{SG1} - |V_{th1}|\right)^2$$
Where:
- $V_{SG1} = V_b - V_{out}$ (source voltage $V_{S1}=V_b$ minus gate voltage $V_{out}$),
- $k_{p1} = \mu_p C_{ox} \frac{W}{L}$ for M1, $|V_{th1}|$ is M1's threshold voltage magnitude.
Substitute (3) into M1's current equation, and solve for $V_{out}$:
$$V_{out} = V_b - |V_{th1}| - \sqrt{\frac{2\left(I_{bias} - I_{in}\right)}{k_{p1}}} \tag{4}$$
---
### DC Operating Relations:
1.  $V_{out}$ **increases** as input current $I_{in}$ increases: higher $I_{in}$ reduces $I_{S1D1}$, reducing $V_{SG1} = V_b - V_{out}$, so $V_{out}$ rises.
2.  $V_X$ tracks $V_{out}$ via the fixed offset from (2): $V_X = V_{out} + V_{th2} + \sqrt{2I_1/k_{n2}}$, so $V_X$ also increases with $I_{in}$.
3.  **Saturation Conditions** (to maintain active region operation):
    - For M1: $V_X \geq V_{out} + |V_{th1}|$, which simplifies to $V_{th2} + \sqrt{2I_1/k_{n2}} \geq |V_{th1}|$, a design constraint on $I_1$ and transistor thresholds.
    - For M2: $V_{DD} - V_{out} \geq V_X - V_{out} - V_{th2}$, which simplifies to $V_{DD} \geq V_X - V_{th2}$, easily satisfied for typical $V_{DD} > V_b > V_X$.
---
## Step 3: Small-Signal Analysis
We calculate the **transimpedance gain** $A_I = v_{out}/i_{in}$ (V/A, output voltage per input current) and output resistance, using small-signal models for the MOSFETs (ideal current sources have infinite small-signal resistance, $V_{DD}$, $V_b$, and current source quiescent currents are AC ground):

    Where:
    - $v_{gs2} = v_X - v_{out}$ (small-signal gate-source voltage),
    - $v_{ds2} = -v_{out}$ (small-signal drain-source voltage, $V_{D2}=V_{DD}$ is AC ground),
    - $g_{m2} = \sqrt{2 k_{n2} I_1}$ (M2's transconductance), $r_{o2} = 1/(\lambda_2 I_1)$ (M2's output resistance).
    KCL (currents leaving $V_{out}$ sum to 0):
    $$g_{m2}(v_X - v_{out}) - \frac{v_{out}}{r_{o2}} = 0 \tag{5}$$
    For $g_{m2} r_{o2} \gg 1$ (typical intrinsic gain), this simplifies to $v_X \approx v_{out}$.
2.  **Input Node $V_X$**:
    Small-signal currents entering $V_X$: $i_{in}$ (input current) and M1's drain current. For M1 (PMOS, saturation):
    $$i_{d1} = -g_{m1} v_{gs1} - \frac{v_{ds1}}{r_{o1}}$$
    Where:
    - $v_{gs1} = v_{out}$ (small-signal gate-source voltage, $V_{S1}=V_b$ is AC ground),
    - $v_{ds1} = v_X$ (small-signal drain-source voltage),
    - $g_{m1} = \sqrt{2 k_{p1} (I_{bias} - I_{in})}$ (M1's transconductance), $r_{o1} = 1/(\lambda_1 (I_{bias} - I_{in}))$ (M1's output resistance).
    KCL (currents entering $V_X$ sum to 0):
    $$i_{in} - g_{m1} v_{out} - \frac{v_X}{r_{o1}} = 0 \tag{6}$$
---
### Transimpedance Gain:
Substitute $v_X \approx v_{out}$ (from (5)) into (6):
$$i_{in} \approx v_{out} \left(g_{m1} + \frac{1}{r_{o1}}\right) \approx g_{m1} v_{out}$$
Since $g_{m1} \gg 1/r_{o1}$ (intrinsic gain $g_{m1} r_{o1} \gg 1$):

---
### Output Resistance:
The small-signal resistance looking into $V_{out}$ is the parallel of M2's output resistance and $I_1$'s output resistance:
$$R_{out} = r_{o2} || R_{I1} \approx r_{o2} = \frac{1}{\lambda_2 I_1}$$
This is a high output resistance, as expected for a current-source-loaded amplifier.
---
## Step 4: Feedback & Performance
- The feedback path ($V_{out} \to$ M1's gate) is **negative feedback**: an increase in $V_{out}$ reduces $I_{S1D1}$, which increases $I_{in}$ to balance KCL, opposing the initial change in $V_{out}$. This stabilizes the operating point and sets the transimpedance gain to ~$1/g_{m1}$.
- The circuit is a **current-input, voltage-output** transimpedance amplifier, with high output resistance, medium input resistance $R_{in} \approx 1/g_{m1}$, and gain set by M1's transconductance.
---
## Final Notes
- If the bias current sink $I_{bias}$ is matched to $I_1$ (current mirror), the quiescent (zero input current) output voltage is $V_{out0} = V_b - |V_{th1}| - \sqrt{2I_1/k_{p1}}$, and the transimpedance gain decreases as $I_{in}$ increases (since $g_{m1}$ decreases with lower $I_{S1D1}$).

To analyze the circuit (a **PMOS current-input feedback transimpedance amplifier**, per the filename, with analysis aligned to the drawn symbol/connection convention, noting the arrow direction matches NMOS operation, with equivalent PMOS analysis noted):
---
## Step 1: Terminal & Connection Identification
The circuit uses 2 MOSFETs (M1, M2), 3 current sources, a supply $V_{DD}$, bias $V_b$, input $I_{in}$, and output $V_{out}$:
### Transistor Terminals (PMOS, per filename, arrow points *into* the source, towards the channel):
1.  **M2 (upper transistor):**
    - Source ($S_2$): Top terminal, connected to $V_{DD}$ (highest potential, correct for PMOS source).
    - Drain ($D_2$): Bottom terminal, connected to $V_{out}$.
    - Gate ($G_2$): Left terminal, connected to feedback node $X$ (common gate node for M1/M2).
2.  **M1 (lower transistor):**
    - Source ($S_1$): Right terminal, connected to bias $V_b$ (high potential, PMOS source).
    - Drain ($D_1$): Top terminal, connected to $V_{out}$.
    - Gate ($G_1$): Left terminal, connected to common gate node $X$.
### Current Sources:
1.  $I_1$: Between $V_{DD}$ and $V_{out}$, arrow down: fixed current source, supplies current *into* $V_{out}$.
2.  $I_{in}$: Between ground and node $X$, arrow up: **independent input current**, sourced into $X$.
3.  $I_{sink}$: Between node $X$ and ground, arrow down: fixed current sink, draws current from $X$ to ground.
### Nodes:
- $V_{out}$: High-impedance output node (open circuit, no external load).
- $X$: Common gate node for M1/M2, input node for $I_{in}$ and $I_{sink}$.
---
## Step 2: DC Operating Point Analysis (Saturation Region)
For PMOS in saturation: $I_D = \frac{1}{2}\mu_p C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}(V_{SG} - |V_{th}|)^2 = K(V_{SG} - V_{th})^2$, where $V_{SG} = V_S - V_G > V_{th}$ (positive overdrive for PMOS), $V_{SD} \geq V_{SG} - V_{th}$.
---
### KCL at $V_{out}$ (sum of currents entering = 0, open circuit):
Currents *leaving* $V_{out}$ (PMOS drain current flows from source to drain, *into* drain, so for $V_{out}$ as drain, current *enters* $V_{out}$; to balance $I_1$ entering $V_{out}$, we define $I_D$ as current *leaving* $V_{out}$ for consistency, or use sign convention where $I_1 = I_{D1} + I_{D2}$):
$$I_1 = I_{D1} + I_{D2} \tag{1}$$
The sum of M1 and M2's drain currents equals the fixed current $I_1$, as $I_1$ is the only current supplied to $V_{out}$.
---
### KCL at Node $X$ (sum of currents entering = 0):
- Currents entering $X$: $I_{in}$ (input current), $I_{D1}$ (source current of M1, flows from $V_b$ to $X$, into $X$), $I_{D2}$ (source current of M2, flows from $V_{DD}$ to $X$, into $X$).
- Currents leaving $X$: $I_{sink}$ (current sink to ground).
$$I_{in} + I_{D1} + I_{D2} = I_{sink} \tag{2}$$
Substitute $I_{D1} + I_{D2} = I_1$ from (1):
$$I_{in} + I_1 = I_{sink} \tag{3}$$
For $I_{in}$ to be an independent input, $I_{sink}$ is a fixed bias current, so this relation holds for the DC operating point, with $I_{D1}$ and $I_{D2}$ adjusting to balance the equation as $I_{in}$ changes.
---
### MOSFET Current-Voltage Relations:
1.  **M1:** $V_{SG1} = V_b - V_X$, where $V_X$ is the voltage at node $X$:
    $$I_{D1} = K_1\left(V_b - V_X - V_{th1}\right)^2 \tag{4}$$
2.  **M2:** $V_{SG2} = V_{DD} - V_X$:
    $$I_{D2} = K_2\left(V_{DD} - V_X - V_{th2}\right)^2 \tag{5}$$
---
### Solve for $V_X$ and $V_{out}$:
From (1) and (2), $I_{D2} = I_{sink} - I_{in} - I_{D1}$, but for matched transistors ($K_1=K_2=K$, $V_{th1}=V_{th2}=V_{th}$), $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_1/2$ if $V_b = V_{DD}$, but for general $V_b$:
From (4), solve for $V_X$:
$$V_X = V_b - V_{th1} - \sqrt{\frac{I_{D1}}{K_1}}$$
From (5), solve for $V_{out}$ using $I_{D2} = I_1 - I_{D1}$:
$$V_{out} = V_{DD} - V_{th2} - \sqrt{\frac{I_1 - I_{D1}}{K_2}}$$
For matched devices, this simplifies to show $V_{out}$ is a function of $I_{in}$, $V_b$, $I_1$, and $I_{sink}$.
---
## Step 3: Feedback Analysis
The feedback path is $V_{out} \to G_2 \to I_{D2} \to V_X \to I_{D1} \to V_{out}$:
1.  If $I_{in}$ *increases*: KCL at $X$ requires $I_{D1} + I_{D2}$ to increase to match $I_{in} + I_{sink}$. Since $I_{D1} + I_{D2} = I_1$ is fixed, this is only possible if $V_{out}$ changes to adjust $V_{SG2}$, hence $I_{D2}$:
    - $I_{in}$ ↑ → $I_{D2}$ ↓ (to keep $I_{D1}+I_{D2}=I_1$) → $V_{SG2} = V_{DD} - V_X$ ↓ → $V_{out}$ ↓ (since $V_{SD2} = V_{DD} - V_{out} \geq V_{SG2} - V_{th}$).
    - Lower $V_{out}$ reduces $V_{SG2}$ further, reducing $I_{D2}$ to counteract the increase in $I_{in}$: this is **negative feedback**, stabilizing the operating point and improving linearity.
---
## Step 4: Small-Signal (AC) Analysis
For small signals around the DC bias, with $V_b, I_1, I_{sink}, V_{DD}$ as AC ground, transimpedance gain $Z_{trans} = v_{out}/i_{in}$ is:
$$Z_{trans} \approx -\frac{1}{g_{m1} + g_{m2}}$$
where $g_{m1,2} = \partial I_{D1,2}/\partial V_{SG1,2} = 2\sqrt{K I_{D1,2}}$ is the transconductance of M1/M2. The negative sign indicates $V_{out}$ decreases as $I_{in}$ increases, consistent with DC behavior.
---
## Final Behavior:
This circuit acts as a **transimpedance amplifier (TIA)**, converting input current $I_{in}$ to output voltage $V_{out}$, with negative feedback providing stable, linear operation. For matched PMOS devices, $V_{out}$ decreases as $I_{in}$ increases, with a gain set by the transistor transconductances and bias currents.
If the transistors are NMOS (as drawn by the arrow direction), the analysis is identical, with $V_{GS}$ replacing $V_{SG}$, and $V_{out}$ referenced to ground instead of $V_{DD}$.
